title: Landing page for families
question: Three ways to build the EducazenKids landing page (the manager dashboard comes next). Pick one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: The tailored report card
options.lineage: the bulletin scolaire every family reads each term
options.thesis: The page reads like a report card rewritten for one child: each subject row shows how EducazenKids teaches it.
options.viewport: A large « Bulletin sur mesure » header for an example student, subject rows with app proof, « Prendre rendez-vous » top right.
options.risk: A report card can feel like judgement; the copy has to stay warm.

options.label: The liaison notebook
options.lineage: the carnet de liaison between school and family
options.thesis: The page is the school-to-family notebook: dated entries from the centre to parents, each one a feature.
options.viewport: An open spread: « Mot aux parents » with the promise and action on the left, the app on a phone clipped to the right page.
options.risk: A paper metaphor can drift into nostalgia if the app stops being central.

options.label: Two screens, one family
options.lineage: the parent's view and the student's phone, side by side
options.thesis: A split page: what the parent wants to know on one side, the student's phone on the other, moving in step.
options.viewport: Left: « Vous suivez, il avance » with the action; right: a live phone that changes screen as you scroll.
options.risk: On phones the split must become stacked moments, or the idea is lost.
